chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Wahb ibn Wahb al-Qurashi, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both), that Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said:
None will be brought up from the earth on the Day of Resurrection except that two angels will be holding him by his arms, saying: Answer the Lord of Glory.

key_terms.تنقش: To be raised/brought up from the earth — referring to resurrection from graves on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.رب العزة: Lord of Glory/Might — a Quranic title of God (cf. 37:180, 38:65) emphasizing His absolute power, majesty, and right to judge
key_terms.ضبعيه: His two arms/armpits — the angels grip from underneath the arms in a manner indicating compulsion and escort

ai.seo_question: What happens to a person when they are raised on the Day of Resurrection according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) describes a vivid eschatological scene: every person raised from the earth on the Day of Resurrection will be accompanied by two angels gripping their arms, summoning them before God, the Lord of Glory. This hadith emphasizes the inescapable nature of divine accountability and the role of angels as escorts at the resurrection. The original audience, familiar with Quranic descriptions of the resurrection, would have understood 'rabb al-'izzah' (Lord of Glory) as a divine title denoting God's absolute majesty and power to judge.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa`d Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Abi `Abdillah from his father from Wahb b. Wahb al-Qurashi from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father (as). `Ali b. Abi Talib (as) said:
None will be brought up from the earth on the Day of Resurrection except that two angels will take him by his arms and say: Answer the Lord of Glory.
